meta.rule: integrated light = the stellar populations' absorption lines (metal lines × m^mz, m = 10^(0.3·[Fe/H])) on the black body of the galaxy's B−V temperature with its 4000-Å break, plus its H II regions' emission lines scaled from its Hα equivalent width; f = c/λ/2^40

units.lines: [label, nm air, drawn width nm, depth old, inter, young, metal exponent]
units.em: [label, nm air, drawn width nm, key, ratio]

meta.note: Every galaxy's spectrum is typical for its kind, shaped by its own measured [Fe/H], B−V and radial velocity and, for the star-forming ones, its Hα strength and H II-region ratios; no whole-galaxy spectrum of any one galaxy is used. APPROX ±30–50 %.

spheroidal.note: old and metal-poor; no gas, so no emission

transition.note: old and intermediate-age stars, a little neutral gas but no H II regions to speak of

irregular.note: young blue stars and their glowing gas

mw.note: seen from outside as a typical Sbc: a bulge's old light and a disc's young light, with modest emission

m31.note: an Sb dominated by its old, metal-rich bulge (K-giant-like); very little star formation, its faint emission with [N II] stronger than Hα as in its bulge's gas

m32.note: a compact elliptical: old, metal-rich stars with an intermediate-age share (stronger Hβ than a giant elliptical); no gas

m110.note: a dwarf elliptical with a few-hundred-Myr-old population in its centre: stronger Balmer lines; almost no gas

ngc185.note: a dwarf elliptical, old and metal-poor; a little dust and gas in the centre but no H II regions to speak of

ngc147.note: a dwarf elliptical, old and metal-poor, no gas

m33.note: an Sc full of young stars and H II regions (NGC 604); its gas a little below solar metallicity

lmc.note: young stars and bright H II regions (30 Doradus); gas at half the Sun's metallicity, so [N II] is weak and [O III] strong

smc.note: young stars and H II regions in gas at a fifth of the Sun's metallicity: [N II] very weak, [O III] strong

ic10.note: the Local Group's starburst dwarf: the strongest emission here (and heavily reddened by our own Galaxy's dust, which is not shown)

ngc6822.note: a dwarf irregular with bright H II regions (Hubble V and X)

ic1613.note: a quiet dwarf irregular: young stars, faint H II regions

wlm.note: a metal-poor dwarf irregular with a few H II regions

sagittariusdsph.note: mostly an intermediate-age, fairly metal-rich population ([Fe/H] −0.4) beside old metal-poor stars; no gas

fornax.note: old and intermediate-age stars ([Fe/H] −1.0), star formation stopped ~100 Myr ago; no gas

carina.note: old and intermediate-age stars from separate bursts; no gas

ngc55.note: a Magellanic-type spiral seen edge-on, star-forming
